Security is the last part of the stack still built on the assumption that a human is watching. Everything else an engineering team touches has already been rebuilt for machine speed. The data warehouse. The deploy pipeline. The code editor itself. Each one got replaced the moment the old, human-paced version turned into the bottleneck. The security operations center is the holdout. It still sits a person in front of a queue & asks them to keep pace with software. Today Cursor goes public as an Artemis Security customer, & it's the clearest sign yet that the holdout is falling. A company operating at Cursor's velocity was never going to route detection & response through a console designed for a slower decade. Artemis now processes 10b+ events daily & resolves 96% of investigations autonomously. The human is left with the fraction that needs judgment, not the fraction a staffing plan happened to allow. This is a category flip, not a one-off vendor swap. The AI-native SOC will do to legacy security tooling what the cloud warehouse did to the on-prem database. Cursor is early. The rest of the market is running the same math right now. We're proud to back Shachar , Dan , & the Artemis team.

Three years ago we started Theory on the thesis that AI would reshape how software gets built, sold, and run. And it did -- but so much faster than anyone expected. AI compresses time. New models ship every 41 days. Companies hit $100M faster than any prior generation. And it's even changed the definition of venture, as Seed rounds stretch as high as $500M. The same compression has moved the market map. When we first launched, the argument was still if model companies would be the airlines of the era. Now, that debate feels quaint amid much larger opportunities: the inference layer to power it all, the AI advertising services to subsidize, the agents that will rewrite operations, cybersecurity to combat the growing attack surface, and even better crypto experiences. The next three years will make these look slow. The most ambitious builders we'll meet are just getting started, & we can’t wait to see what they do. https://lnkd.in/gfNaAkht

Tech events have come a long way. Went to one this weekend. Porsche wrapped in company branding at the entrance, two more you could sign up to take a ride around a short circuit, food trucks, free merch. On top of that, all the companies hosting the event had their tents set up. The engineers and even the founders were just standing there. You could easily walk up and start a conversation. That's the coolest thing about these events, in person, everyone is so much more approachable. If you're in the Bay and not going to these, you're sleeping. Just go on Luma and check out the upcoming events in SF for the week. What's the best event you've been to recently?

I feel like a lot of people in SF haven't touched grass in weeks. I was one of them. Took 3 hours off to hike Mount Tam this weekend. If you're deep in the tech/startup world, go outside, it helps It's easy to forget there's a world outside of AI and funding rounds. Everyone's building something, and the culture kind of rewards never stopping. But the constant grind can lead to burnout. Sometimes your best ideas don't come from staring at a screen. So take a break, three hours outside can do more for your output than three hours of forcing it. The Bay Area has some of the best trails in the country right next to the city. For the others in the Bay right now, what are some other hiking trails I should check out? lmk :)

Artemis Security 🤝 Datadog We treat AI agent performance and cost like any other production signal: instrumented, alerted, and continuously reviewed. Efficiency is not a side quest for an AI-native company. It is what lets us keep giving customers more capabilities without increasing the cost. We built Artemis to run at machine speed, which means AI touches nearly every part of the platform. So we instrumented it the way we instrument everything else, with Datadog Agent Observability across more than 20 dimensions: customer, workflow, investigation type, model, pipeline stage. The result is discipline. Cost regressions surface in under an hour instead of a day. Automated monitors catch routing and catch issues before they incur impact. Thanks to the Datadog team for the partnership! Full case study in the comments.
